have heinv : μ.map e.symm=μ := by
    have H := congrArg (fun ν : Measure Y => ν.map e.symm) he
    rw [Measure.map_map e.symm.measurable e.measurable] at H
    simpa only [Function.comp_def,e.symm_apply_apply,Measure.map_id'] using H.symm
  apply bind_eq_of_real_integrals
  intro A hA
  have hEA : MeasurableSet (e ⁻¹' A) := hA.preimage e.measurable
  calc
    _ = ∫ x, (κ (e.symm x)).real (e ⁻¹' A) ∂μ := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact ae_of_all _ fun x => congrArg ENNReal.toReal (by
        rw [transportKernel_apply,Measure.map_apply e.measurable hA])
    _ = ∫ x, (κ x).real (e ⁻¹' A) ∂μ := by
      change (∫ x, (κ (e.symm x) (e ⁻¹' A)).toReal ∂μ)=_
      rw [←integral_map e.symm.measurable.aemeasurable
        (κ.measurable_coe hEA).ennreal_toReal.aestronglyMeasurable,heinv]
      rfl
    _ = (μ.bind κ).real (e ⁻¹' A) := (bind_kernel_real κ μ _ hEA).symm
    _ = μ.real A := by

      exact congrArg ENNReal.toReal ((Measure.map_apply e.measurable hA).symm.trans

findings.problem: The measure equality takes an unnecessary detour through real-valued integrals, introducing toReal conversions, almost-everywhere congruence, and strong measurability bookkeeping. The same change-of-variables argument works directly with the ENNReal-valued integrals defining bind.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the proof body with:
by
  have heinv : μ.map e.symm = μ := by
    simpa only [he] using e.map_symm_map (μ := μ)
  ext A hA
  have hEA : MeasurableSet (e ⁻¹' A) := hA.preimage e.measurable
  calc
    μ.bind (transportKernel e κ) A
        = ∫⁻ x, κ (e.symm x) (e ⁻¹' A) ∂μ := by
          rw [Measure.bind_apply hA
            (transportKernel e κ).measurable.aemeasurable]
          simp only [transportKernel_apply, Measure.map_apply e.measurable hA]
    _ = ∫⁻ x, κ x (e ⁻¹' A) ∂μ := by
      rw [← lintegral_map (κ.measurable_coe hEA) e.symm.measurable, heinv]
    _ = (μ.bind κ) (e ⁻¹' A) :=
      (Measure.bind_apply hEA κ.measurable.aemeasurable).symm
    _ = μ A := by
      rw [hstat, ← Measure.map_apply e.measurable hA, he]
findings.benefit: Keeps the same explicit mathematical steps—evaluate the transported kernel, change variables, apply stationarity, and use invariance—without the real-integral machinery. All original assumptions can remain, and zero measures and empty spaces require no special treatment.

theorem bind_apply {m : Measure α} {f : α → Measure β} {s : Set β} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (hf : AEMeasurable f m) : bind m f s = ∫⁻ a, f a s ∂m := by

theorem lintegral_map {f : β → ℝ≥0∞} {g : α → β} (hf : Measurable f)
    (hg : Measurable g) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂map g μ = ∫⁻ a, f (g a) ∂μ := by

theorem map_symm_map (e : α ≃ᵐ β) : (μ.map e).map e.symm = μ := by
  simp [map_map e.symm.measurable e.measurable]

theorem map_apply (hf : Measurable f) {s : Set β} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    μ.map f s = μ (f ⁻¹' s) :=
  map_apply_of_aemeasurable hf.aemeasurable hs

protected theorem measurable_coe (κ : Kernel α β) {s : Set β} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    Measurable fun a => κ a s :=
  (Measure.measurable_coe hs).comp κ.measurable
